scientific_hypothesis: A multi-cavity design using SiO2 and Al2O3 with three defect layers will produce sharper bandpass edges than a single-cavity design, enabling better separation between the 255-280 nm passband and the 300+ nm stopbands.
expected_advantages: Sharper bandpass edges improve stopband rejection near passband
SiO2 and Al2O3 have minimal UV absorption
Flat-top passband better covers the full 255-280 nm range
known_risks: Three cavities increase optimization complexity and risk of local minima
May be more sensitive to thickness errors than single-cavity design
expected_observations: If the hypothesis holds, best_target_score should show improved edge steepness (transition from 280 nm to 300 nm) compared to route_01, and tightest_margin should remain stable.
If the hypothesis fails, best_target_score will not exceed route_01 despite higher layer count, indicating the multi-cavity complexity does not pay off for this wavelength combination.
thicknesses_nm should show three distinct cavity layers with approximately half-wave optical thickness if mode coupling is achieved.
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best.
If valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, reduce the layer count by removing one mirror pair from each Bragg section and continue for one more round before stopping.
